attributes.residual: NO CODE RESIDUAL. THE TOOL FINDING, which is why this record exists beyond the two rules: the CR record warned that `wf_word_diff` calls this residual `CLASS: RECOLOR` by index alignment and told the rule author not to write a recolor. THE TOOL HAS SINCE BEEN REFINED AND THE WARNING STILL STANDS, in a weaker but still misleading form. Measured this run on both twins: it now prints `CLASS: RECOLOR-SHAPED BUT NOT RECOLOURABLE -- the streams are index-aligned (0 mnemonic divergence), which is what the old CLASS line read, but 2 RA-ZERO word(s) sit outside the register-field class`, with `DECODE: REGFIELD-ONLY 0, RA-ZERO 2, ... 2 of 2 word(s) lie OUTSIDE every register-field class`, and it closes by suggesting `The addi li<->copy subset is reachable with an equivalent_copy_form arrow, not with a register-field rule`. So the refinement fixed the CLASS verdict -- it no longer says a recolor closes this -- while leaving the CURE wrong: an `equivalent_copy_form` arrow re-encodes the TARGET's encoding around OUR registers at ONE site, and there is no site here to re-encode. The two words are `addi r4,r3,0 @lbl_8025776C(ADDR16_LO)` and `li r5,0`, two DIFFERENT instructions that traded places; the RA-ZERO reading is an artefact of pairing them by index, since `li r5,0` is `addi r5,r0,0` and its literal-zero rA is what the decoder reports. The residual is a two-atom SWAP and only the permutation stage reaches it. GENERALISATION, and the reason this is worth a record rather than a footnote: an index-aligning word comparison cannot distinguish a two-instruction transposition from a two-word rewrite, in EITHER direction, and both of its verdicts on such a pair -- the old RECOLOR and the new RA-ZERO/copy-form -- point the author at a stage that cannot work. The arbiter for the distinction is the aligned `fnasm --raw --diff` view, which shows the `>` / `<` displacement rows the word diff has no way to emit.

denial.falsifier: Any source form of either twin that reorders those two preheader instructions while holding 104/104 and 108/108. Two directions are already measured to fail and are not falsifiers: a form that reorders them by changing the address expression (the raw byte-offset base is REQUIRED -- naming it costs two instructions), and a form that reorders them by changing the loop shape (the do/while costs the ctr loop's entry guard). A falsifier has to move the preheader ORDER without touching either.

ADDR16_LO` before the `li r5,0` on both twins, at T104/O104 and T108/O108 respectively. hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Zero builds: grep the image for the other readers of `lbl_8025776C` and, for each, run `fnasm.py <unit> <fn> <preheader> --raw --diff`. If no third reader exists, or every reader shows the same displacement, the census is empty and this hypothesis dies immediately at no cost. If one reader emits `li` first, diff its source against the twins' `case 7:` block and the answer is in that diff.
hypothesis.count_consequence: Any cure must hold T104/O104 and T108/O108. This pair has now lost parity on TWO separate source axes -- the named base at O102 and the loop form at O103 -- so parity is the first thing to read on any probe here, not the last, and a count move ends the axis immediately per claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1. The census in the hypothesis above is count-neutral by construction, since it compiles nothing.

hypothesis.statement: The promotion route is a SIBLING, not another probe on these two. Both twins scan the same table with the same idiom and both emit the two preheader instructions in the same wrong order, which means the order is a property of the IDIOM -- `sprintf`-into-a-table-scan seeded from an `lbl_` base with a ctr loop -- and not of either function. If a THIRD function in the image compiles the same idiom and gets the order RIGHT, the difference between it and these two is the source form nobody has found in seven records. That is a census question, not a probe question, and it has never been asked.
